This endpoint redacts amounts, quantities, account numbers and the names taken off statements (merchants, payers, narratives), and shows a name a person typed about an account as a pseudonym such as manual-1, or as its account number, redacted; source ids, other account names, holdings and their names, categories and shares stay visible. Amounts and quantities print as *****.** and ***, account numbers keep only their last digits, and merchant, payer and narrative text prints as ***. A name a person typed about an account prints as a pseudonym: a nickname, an account category the config sets, and the names and ids of crypto, manual and declared accounts and portfolios and their line ids. The name of an account its bank names by its nickname is typed too. An account whose name is typed shows its account number instead, redacted, where that number is letters and digits with at least one digit; so does such an id. A pseudonym is a prefix and a number: the source's kind (manual-1, cointracking-2), or category-1 and nickname-1. Within one result a value always reads the same pseudonym, and two values read apart. Each call numbers afresh: manual-1 in two different calls need not be one value, so join results on other columns. A call numbers over all its rows before filters and paging, so the same call with a filter added names a row as before. A source id names a config entry and stays legible, as does a name another provider builds from the holder's words. A holding's name stays legible. A hand-entered holding's key and instrument id redact as an account number, their words kept; an id typed into its name, or into an issuer or a cash flow line named after it, masks, and the name's words stay. Other account names, holdings and their symbols, dates, categories, types, classes and shares stay legible.
Filters and sorts read what is shown: a money column cannot order the rows here, a merchant filter matches nothing, and a filter or search matches a typed name by its pseudonym, the whole cell (manual-1 never matches manual-10).
